item.title: SCP draft- Ancient Nautiloids
item.description: Four nautiloids from the Atlantic undiscovered for centuries by mankind.
item.content:encoded:
+ show block
– hide block

SCP-XXXX

Object Class: Euclid

Special Containment Procedures: Due to the various populations of SCP-XXXX being spread out in the Atlantic Ocean, SCP-XXXX instances are to be monitored by multiple research vessels. Only personnel with a marine biology background or naval background are allowed to monitor SCP-XXXX instances.

ROVs or dive crews are permitted to observe SCP-XXXX instances. Dive teams must keep a distance of 5-10 when approaching. If the observing instance of SCP-XXXX shows no interest to personnel, personnel shouldn’t attempt to follow or surrounding SCP-XXXX instances will flee.

Should eggs be discovered, divers or ROVs should be sent on a monthly basis to monitor the egg depending on the depth of the water. Monitoring should end when all eggs are hatched. Unhatched eggs are to be collected for observation.

Washed-up carcasses or shells of SCP-XXXX instances must be removed from the location discovered. Any person of the public must be treated with amnestics after the confiscation of items. Info of the SCP from outside researchers and media must be confiscated immediately to prevent public curiosity. A cover story must be formed after doing so.

If the ritual battle of SCP-XXXX instances would occur, ships controlled by the foundation must set up a perimeter of a radius of 10 kilometers around the center of the Bermuda Triangle. The perimeter can only disperse when the battle is over and the lone instance of SCP-XXXX has left.

Description: SCP-5181 is a designation of 4 species of nautiloids located around the world. They are designated as SCP-XXXX-A to D. Each one is vastly different from the other.

SCP-XXXX-A are conical-shelled nautiloids with a shell length of 4 meters. Resembling an Orthoceras in physique, SCP-XXXX-A’s arms are 1.5 meters long. The skin of this instance is maroon. The color of the shell is a dark shade of brown with orange stripes.

SCP-XXXX-A are migratory in nature. They live in the North Atlantic for the summers before heading south in the fall. Instances of SCP-XXXX-A return to the north in mid-April.

SCP-XXXX-B are curved-shelled nautiloids with a shell length of 1.5 meters. At a meter up the shell, a blade-like protrusion is apparent that starts 20cm from the shel’s basel. Arms of this instance are hooked and 70cm long each. A thin line of webbing about 20cm from the base is present on SCP-XXXX-B. The shell protrusion is sharp enough to slice prey when the instance SCP-XXXX-B rams into it.

Instances of SCP-XXXX-B are observed to live in the open waters in the Caribbean Sea. From observation, SCP-XXXX-B rams itself into schools of fish. Fish are either cut by the protrusion or incapacitated by the shell.

SCP-XXXX-C are nautiloids 1 meter in diameter resembling a chambered nautilus in physique. The shell is a charcoal grey coloring with grooves where the walls of the chambers are located. Its skin coloring is primarily navy blue. Instances of SCP-XXXX-C are capable of emitting cyan-colored bioluminescence at the ends of their tentacles.

SCP-XXX-C live in benthic environments near submarine canyons of the Atlantic ocean that lead to open waters. SCP-XXXX-C will outstretch its arms radially and emit its bioluminescence. Prey is hypnotized and is compelled to come close. From there, SCP-XXXX-C will wrap its tentacles around the prey before consuming.

SCP-XXXX-D are coiled-shelled nautiloids that are approximately shell diameter of 2 meters. The shell is a gradient of orange and yellow with a black stone-like outer layer. The pattern of the shell is supposed to resemble cooling lava. Arms are 5 meters long from the base to the tip. All tentacles have microscopic hairs on them. This suggests instances of SCP-XXXX-D can feed similar to yeti crabs.

SCP-XXXX-D instances are seen near hydrothermal vents off in the Mid-Atlantic Ridge. The instances of SCP-XXXX-D are very slow-moving due to the weight of the shell. Though capable of catching prey, it prefers to harvest bacteria for chemosynthesis. After the synthesis is sufficient, it will eat the bacteria.

All instances of SCP-XXXX reach sexual maturity at around 10 years. Each female instance lays a clutch of 10-30 eggs. The eggs are hard and soft as leather. Gestation period of the eggs is about 10-12 months. Once hatched, instances of SCP-XXXX will have a yolk to survive on for the first two weeks of life. Hatchlings look like miniature versions of their adult forms. A small yolk is present when the instances are born. After two weeks, the yolk is used up and the offspring are ready to hunt for themselves.

Every 10 years in around mid to late April, at least one instance of each instance of SCP-XXXX will meet at the center of the Bermuda Triangle. Once all of the instances are gathered, they all fight to the death. The fight will only end after there’s a sole survivor of the death match. The sole survivor will leave the battle to return to its home.

After the battle the population of the instance significantly grows for the next three years. The boom in population of the winning instance is likely due to the instances of SCP-XXXX reaching sexual maturity at the same amount of time. It’s theorized that the battles are some kind of ritual for fertility rights.

Discovery
Instances of SCP-XXXX were discovered in April 2005 by an international oceanography survey. On sonar, they discovered four blips near the center of the Bermuda Triangle. The survey team stopped at about a kilometer to not spook what creatures were there. Divers are sent after the ships stopped moving.

According to the divers witnessing the event, there was at least one individual of each SCP-XXXX instance. All of the instances were attacking each other disregarding their own wellbeing. After the battle, only the instance of SCP-XXXX-B left the battle alive, albeit barely.

After testimonies of the crew were given, amnestics were administered to them. Footage and logs of SCP-XXXX were confiscated and destroyed after copying data to the foundation database.

Addendum XXXX-1
After analyzing the shells, only the shells of SCP-XXXX-B and SCP-XXXX-D have abnormalities. Traces of Iron are found where the protrusion SCP-XXXX-B. The protrusion itself is about 85% iron.

The rock growths on SCP-XXXX-D’s shell have properties of pumice but of unknown composition. It is theorized that the pumice-like rocks help with SCP-XXXX-D to maintain buoyancy.

Addendum XXXX-2
The captivity of SCP-XXXX instances is impossible at this point in time. All instances have died during transport or within hours of being settled in a theoretically suitable enclosure.

Addendum XXXX-3
On April 20, 2015, another battle among the SCP-XXXX instances occurred. The weather at the time was mostly cloudy with high winds. Monitoring of the battle was difficult due to the rising waves. The instance of SCP-XXXX-D was declared the victor by the foundation after the shells of the other instances were discovered.


Please dont post drafts to the forums.

item.title: Null tower
item.description: A spiral stairwell underneath a lighthouse
item.content:encoded:
Seeking Greenlights: Yes

Page Type: SCP Article

Elevator Pitch: SCP-XXXX Is a spiral stairwell underneath a lighthouse located outside of Koror, Palau. The stairwell contains writings written with plantlife in an unknown language. Anybody can read it, but no cognitohazards have been identified.
Near the bottom of the stairwell is an entity observed to write the text on the walls. It has an appearance similar to a wendigo glowing a bright white color. people to entity as "the Null walker" when never given its name. It's docile but can cause illusions to provokers.
At the bottom of the stairwell is a bioluminescent cave with more text and unidentified life.

Central Narrative: In the first exploration, a D-Class was to record the texts and descend as low as he can. He was able to find the Null walker, but what happened next was unknown.
In the second exploration log, a 3 man MTF team was to continue exploration with better equipment. 5 hours in, the leader of the MTF goes into the stairwell alone and tells nobody to follow him. After 30 minutes, he is found to have committed suicide by gunshot, with a note saying that the Null walker will reincarnate him and keep him from harm. The next day he was found continuing his daily routine, with no recollection of the event.
A 4 person MTF team was to have a more permanent exploration in the final exploration log. A Cognito hazard specialist, Linguistic, Anomalous biologist, and a psychologist were sent. The cognitohazard specialist and the linguist went missing, and later the linguist was found dead and killed by the Cognitohazard specialist (who is missing). The biologist and the psychologist team up and cut off the connection to control. One month later, they are also found in their daily routine with no recollection of the event.
In the end, they find journals belonging to the biologist and previous MTFs. In the biologist's journal, she talks about how she and the psychologist looked out for each other and how they killed the cognitohazard specialist. After they went down to the bottom of the stairwell and found the giant bioluminescent cave and the D-classes' animated bodies and the previous MTF, were glowing blue and showed no intelligence.

Hook/Attention-Grabber: This SCP gives an urge for both the foundation and the readers to find out what is at the bottom of the stairwell.

Additional Notes: 400-word limit, ask questions so I answer

item.title: My Eternal Crusade
item.description: A lone, indestructible crusader on an impossible quest.
item.content:encoded:
Seeking Greenlights: Yes

Page Type: SCP Article

Elevator Pitch: An indestructible and immortal crusader is on a quest to rid the world of SCP's either by killing them or cleansing them of their "corruption."

+ show block
– hide block

Central Narrative: An MTF Squad is out looking for an SCP that had escaped containment, but instead end up finding the Crusader after having just killed it. They take him into custody, and quickly realize just what they have found and make a deal with him. Discovering unlike other SCP's, once you take away his "blessed" weapons and shield he's just your everyday, immortal, above average human male wearing crusader armor, the Foundation makes him an offer. He begrudgingly agrees and helps the Foundation to capture or kill dangerous SCP’s. Twice, when sent on a mission to capture a new SCP, the Crusader disobeys orders, killing one SCP but helping another escape before letting either one be identified. The second time becomes the last straw, and when questioned, it becomes apparent that up to this point all that mattered was his quest, but this is a much more personal matter that he refuses to share with the Foundation. The only things he ends up telling the Foundation is that many others also believed the knowledge they would gain would outweigh the danger, and that not all birds were meant to be caged.

Hook/Attention-Grabber: The Foundation is always seeking anti anomalous SCP's to help contain other SCP's or put down dangerous ones. But are they willing to compromise and negotiate to achieve that goal? Would they set aside their own beliefs, ideals, and processes for ultimately the greater good, or choose to lose such an asset for the sake of doing things their way? At what point, will they refuse to compromise any further?

Additional Notes: While I’m a fast learner, I don’t have the time or the will to go through every SCP Article, Tale, and Group of Interest. If something here has already been done, or is too similar to something else please let me know.

item.title: Dimensional Snow
item.description: A homemade snow experiment that shows every dimension.
item.content:encoded:
Seeking Greenlight: Yes

Page Type: SCP Article

Elevator Pitch: Each Snowflake produced represents a Dimension.

Central Narrative: The foundation discovers the SCP in 1980 after a man commit's suicide in his house. The foundation found a homemade snowflake experiment that produced snow via unknown means. Continued research produced the idea that each snowflake represented a single dimension which was proven via the foundations making major changes in other dimensions.

Hook/Attention Grabber: Each snowflake represents a single dimension and has been ever increasing since discovery. Any changes made to the dimension will change its represented snowflake and destruction of the snowflake will cause the destruction of its represented universe. The foundation is yet to discover how these snowflakes have connected the dimensions but have noticed that any interference from an outside source tends to change how much a snowflake looks like one another (If the foundation changes a Dimension, the snowflakes of each will highly resemble each other).

Additional Notes: Each snowflake represents its own version of reality and changes based on changes that occur in said dimension.

item.title: Deer in the mist (seeking greenlights)
item.description: Albino deer that distracts humans and kills them, wanting revenge for the many deer killed by humans accidentally.
item.content:encoded:
Seeking Greenlights: Yes
Page Type: SCP Article

+ Elevator Pitch.
- Hide.

Elevator pitch: A creature taking the form of an albino deer, with splattered human blood on its legs. The creature is only documented to have appeared to humans between midnight and 4 am. Often, surrounding the deer, a thick mist will appear, which is the cause of most deaths associated with it, as the mist is too thick for a human to see, and most often the cause of the death is a car crash or being run over by a car. Adorning the creature's antlers are a couple of flowers, appearing as whatever flowers the viewer would consider most beautiful, leading to disagreements on what flowers they are.

+ Central Narrative.
- Hide.

Central Narrative: side note: Interviews with the deer are possible, as it can communicate telepathically with humans. This is translated into the language(s) used in the person's head. The deer has a hatred for humanity, and is not cooperative during interviews, but some information can be extracted from it. When recording all deaths associated with SCP-XXXX, the deer seems to target a specific family (although it doesn't kill only them). It should be noted that this family has a long history of hunting, usually deer. Many from this family have been found with gunshot wounds all over their bodies, after witnessing SCP-XXXX. It has been confirmed that other hnters ad acted on an impulse to shoot when they saw something move in the mist. One of the victims has a diary, in which the last page written describes what happened before his death, seemingly written as it happened.

+ Hook/Attention Grabber.
- Hide.

Hook/Attention-Grabber: The ironic nature of the deaths by the SCP - the fact that the majority of victims were killed by vehicle-related incidents (the second-biggest killers of deer, after hunting), for example. (-and, I suppose, the fact that it's based on an event that happened to my friend, albeit a much more minor event than what is described here.)


Additional Notes: I don't have a sandbox page for this at the time of writing (I probably will make one after I finish online school, I'm on a break). Also, this is based on a story one of my friends told me: she and her brother were out in the middle of the night, and they got jump-scared by a white deer.

item.title: The Blind Researcher
item.content:encoded:
Seeking Greenlights: Yes
Page Type: SCP article
Genre: Slightly leaning towards horror, but not really. A bit similar to Cain/Plague doctor genre.
Elevator pitch: An odd Researcher. She seems to have lived for an unnatural amount of time, possible millennia, and seems to know know everything that has happened in the past or is happening in the present, and always states that she is conducting research. She creates objects, often anomalous, for her research. These substances disappear when she has finished her research on that substance. She states that she wants to help the universe and all the universes, but refuses to divulge anything more than that on what her research
Central Narrative: A sample of a previously believed impossible to create chemical substance by geological researchers in the Gobi desert. This sample was claimed by a young blind woman in a lab coat, who appeared to be able to see despite her lack of eyes. When she was denied the request, she created another sample instead. Due to this, she was reported to the SCP. When confronted, she went willingly, saying "Hmm, this may help with my research. I always wanted to find more about some anomalies." She seems to know about the existence of every SCP and all secret information, despite never being informed. She creates anomalous objects to conduct often bizarre research on, seemingly out of nowhere, and has a journal which she records her findings on. This journal has many anomalous properties, but all that is written on it is basic, third-grade arithmetic. Though she is generally amiable and helpful, she refuses to divulge any information on what her research is, saying that the SCP researchers will not understand, except that it is for good. Every so often, she requests to meet another SCP, which is always denied.
Hook/Attention grabber: A researcher, whom no one understands what her research is, while creating bizarre anomalies in the path of her research. Also, she knows almost everything about every SCP, which creates quite a unique threat.

item.title: Robot Refugees From Outer Space
item.description: {Insert clickbaity captions here}
item.content:encoded:
Seeking Greenlights: Yes

Page Type: SCP Article

Genre (Optional): Drama/Emotional, Action

Elevator Pitch: Three extraterrestrial lifeforms mechanical in nature claiming to be millions of years old and a machine they refer to as "The Forge" have been recently detained. Apparently they are the last remaining members of their species, and the Forge is their last hope of saving it. The Forge is a highly advanced piece of technology that is the robots' main method of reproduction, able to practically 3D print new members of their species under the correct circumstances. According to the three, Earth has the perfect conditions to incubate the Forge. However, the Forge supplies itself with the materials necessary to undergo such processes by absorbing and thaumaturgically converting large amounts of matter. Due to the catastrophic implications of letting a machine like this function on Earth, consuming the world's resources, the Foundation has concluded that the Forge must be destroyed ASAP before a GH-O 'Dead Greenhouse' Scenario could occur. There is only one problem, though: the Forge is nigh-indestructible by conventional means. But the Foundation is quickly looking into ways of solving this problem.

Central Narrative: The three aliens learn they must race against the clock to breach containment, secure the Forge, and escape the Foundation before the machine is destroyed, sealing their species' fate for good. However, if they successfully incubate the Forge on Earth, it could very well mean the end of organic life as we know it.

Hook/Attention-Grabber: Readers will be intrigued by the extensive worldbuilding of the SCPs and their backstories, as well as interesting characters. They will want to find out what will happen to the Forge and the three aliens, and how the story will end. No matter whose side they're on, the story will grip them, pulling them in, compelling them to see this story to the end. Best of all, this whole narrative is neatly packaged into the clinical tone the wiki's readers know and love!

Additional Notes: I would like to hear your thoughts, suggestions, and critiques on the narrative aspect of my SCP article

item.title: Ovda Regio - Aphrodite
item.description: Strange signals coming from the Aphrodite landmass, specifically the Ovda Regio, in Venus.
item.content:encoded:
Seeking Greenlights: Yes

Page Type: SCP Article/GoI

Genre (Optional): Galactic, Mystery

Page Layout (Optional): ACS header, basic layout, and exploration logs.

Elevator Pitch: Venus, a dead toxic planet believed to have no life on it, just sent signals to the SCP foundation, and no one knows who or why they did it, but they'll find out one way or another.

Central Narrative: (SCP) The SCP is currently classified as a signal, mainly because the origin is not yet located, and no one knows where it's precise location is, besides the fact it's located in the Ovda Regio, a massive landform (5280 km) located in the Aphrodite landmass. No one knows if it's a lost tribe, a massive monster, or a distress signal. Signals usually come in an unknown translation of code, and impossible to decipher.

(GoI) The team designated to the Ovda Regio is the ORET (Ovda Regio Exploration Team). They are responsible for scanning the OR in search of the origin of the signal, hoping they don't die from the harsh elements. Because of the toxic environment, limited time on the ground, and the amount of knowledge about the lands, the origin will take a very long time to locate, and has a possibility of not being found at all.

Hook/Attention-Grabber: The most interesting part will 100% be the exploration logs, as there are an abundance of them, and they all are full of interesting content.

Additional Notes: If you want to know what the Ovda Regio is, here's a link. https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Ovda_Regio

item.title: An Obsession with 4 (Looking for a Greenlight)
item.description: causes those with abnormal amount of limbs (4) to be obsessed
item.content:encoded:
Neural Affliction that causes those with abnormal amount of limbs (4) to be obsessed with the aforementioned number to anomalous lengths.

I moved and trimmed your thread summary, since it was taking up extra space in the main forum screen. Try to keep thread descriptions (the text in the little box under the thread title) and titles short so you don't crowd out other authors in the forum listing. ~Zyn

Seeking Greenlights: Yes

Page Type: SCP Article

Elevator Pitch: This is a mind affecting SCP that shares some similarities to OCD, however it's manifestation and extreme cases caused it to be classified as anomalous. Essentially any person who has 4 of some body part, that is not considered "normal" (e.g. 4 fingers or toes) will have a strange obsession with the number 4, often achieving strange and often anomalous actions in pursuit of this goal. The length of the obsession can vary wildly and rarely be something dangerous

Central Narrative: The article will cover how this disease was discovered, as beforehand it was just assumed to be a form of OCD. A serial killer was detained after maiming several victims, as well as grafting various body parts onto himself so that he had four of many vital parts. This was considered anomalous as all grafted body parts (eyes, ears, some organs) were fully functional despite being crudely sewed or stapled to their body. item.title: Hearts and minds?
item.description: To what extent does the Foundation care about hearts and minds, or morality in general?
item.content:encoded:
Now, I know the obvious answer is no, they don't care about hearts and minds. The Foundation is an organization based on the utmost secrecy and regular commits atrocious acts against relatively innocent civilians, so outside of the Broken Masquerade canon they don't concern themselves with a public image.

But what I'm asking about is do they care about the hearts and minds of their own people? Many articles suggest they do to some extent. The entire point of SCP-231 is how far the Foundation is willing to go and the psychological toll it takes on their personnel. So to what extent does morality dictate their actions?

Suppose an MTF is on a mission and one of their guys gets grabbed by something. Mission Control can tell from his vitals that he's injured but still alive, maybe he's even calling for help over the radio. I feel like on any ordinary military mission, rescuing an injured teammate would take priority, but if the Foundation sent in a team then chances are they're already prepared to lose them all. So what would they do? Would they shut off the downed agent's radio and instruct the team to continue the mission? Can they expect their agents to be loyal if they know the Foundation won't bother to save them if they get in trouble? If there are any articles that feature a situation like this, please feel free to tell me, I'd love to read them.

And another thing, do SCP objects that are more subjectively "evil" get treated as higher risks? For example, would an entity like SCP-4666 that targets children be a higher priority than other uncontained SCPs simply because humans are more protective of their young?

I apologize if this is a conversation that's been had before, but the internal morality of the Foundation is a subject that fascinates me, and I'd love to hear people's thoughts on it. Thanks!

item.title: Tectonic Watchers

item.content:encoded:

Page Type: SCP Article.

Page Layout (Optional): An SCP article which is formed as more of a narrative, with reoccurring updates to the SCP itself's sheet. (Think SCP-5000.)

Elevator Pitch: An unexplained (yet theorized) scientific phenomena referred to as "Earthquake lights". Strange lights that seem to appear in the skies whilst (usually high-magnitude) earthquakes form. However, what isn't expected is that these are entities made of light, appearing to simply spectate the earthquakes. Why they do this is found out in the tale.

+ show block
– hide block

Central Narrative: During a high-magnitude earthquake near Site [REDACTED], there were "Earthquake Lights" spotted by many people. As this is a scientifically unexplained phenomena, MTF Unit Rho-10 "Shaken, Not Stirred" (an MTF unit created to withstand seismic activity, or unnatural geological movement) enters the scene to investigate. After recordings are taken, and the film is placed through numerous filters & intensive analyzation, it's found that each of these 'strobes' of light contain an indescribable entity seemingly of extreme brightness (think a Lovecraftian entity), which just so happens to be entity an which seems to be watching the earthquakes. When another high-magnitude earthquake occurs near the same area within the next month, the same dispatch is sent to investigate these flashes of light closer.
As the protagonist, code-name "Charlie-0" (or C-0 by military alphabets) approaches towards the light, it seems to remain still for much longer than previous. They go to the top of the nearest destroyed building via an extremely long grappling hook and a lot of climbing. 23 minutes later, they arrive at the top, before the entity slowly floats down towards him. They take him somewhere - yet to be discovered. The man would slowly begin to communicate with these entities, finding out more and more about them - as the secrets reveal he continually updates the logs manually. The MTF Unit shows development by originally only interacting with the entities for research purposes, however slowly grows to empathize with the fact that they regret their nature. These entities don't wish to create and spectate the chaos which happens, however as if an addiction they depend on it. It is unknown whether they die if there is no chaos spectated. He empathizes, as he was originally a drug addict who severely struggled to break his addiction. He gains motivation to learn more about them to try and find a way to have the foundation assist in this 'chaos'-addiction, as that's what he always wished he had. This also motivates him to write more so the foundation can understand as much as they can.
These light creatures are entities born from dying stars, and as such are naturally attracted towards extremely chaotic events, living off of the chaos. Due to the fact that it's one of the few places which are inhabited, these entities seem to enjoy the chaos which comes with this. When times are extremely boring, they seem to create their own manual disasters, usually by moving tectonic plates and creating earthquakes. as they're the easiest to create.
After they allow him to leave, he goes to the SCP Foundation with all the logged knowledge, discussion, and updates to the file, explaining everything he's learnt (almost everything there is to know). By the end, the SCP Foundation sends him back as a sort of 'messenger' to attempt to create a peace treaty. After this offering for peace, the SCPs seem to at first oblige. For the next year there are no earthquake lights spectated. However, they seem to continue after this time - seemingly more severe then previously, as if something of a relapse. This'd be a whole 'nother stress for the foundation, and I'd need to choose what they'd do after this. As they're aware they would be unable to defeat these entities, the most they can do is attempt to lower the amount of damage caused by SCP-XXXX-1 related earthquakes, and cover up the phenomena as something which it is not.

Hook/Attention-Grabber: The fact that this could, hypothetically, be real is a big thing. Playing off of real world unexplained phenomena. Not to mention the fact it opens up as a tale-SCP has always caught my interest. Another main hook is the fact that these creatures seem to have a society, and people they care about, along with emotions and feeling. It gives a side to them other than just 'chaos-lovers'.

Additional Notes: There is almost definitely some shit which I've messed up with the lore, as I am an idiot. Please feel free to be harsh in critique. Thank you!

The article mentions that highly secret details of the Foundation were leaked on YouTube and iTunes and the efforts to cover up the iTunes incident were imperfect.

It stands to reason then, that maybe some sheltered person hiding behind a sophisticated proxy, or something, managed to download and listen to the songs without having his memory erased, or even being noticed by the Foundation.

I feel that a story following this character as he becomes obsessed trying to get to the bottom of the SCP foundation would be an interesting read.

Central Narrative: I believe the protagonist of this tale would perhaps be some kind of techno-master who spends hours delving into the internet for obscure media. Someone who would notice a strange new album from Tupac appearing on Beyoncé’s iTunes page before it got taken down. The type of guy whose basement is filled with GPUs mining Bitcoin.

I think it would also make sense for this character to be as “off grid” as possible while still having internet access. So he hears about these songs, that sound a lot like Tupac, that are supposedly revealing deeply hidden truths about the world and he pounces on it. Buys the album without a second thought, backs up the songs on multiple drives, and devotes endless effort to figuring out what they mean.

This character would then go on a journey trying to access SCP facilities and finding whatever clues he can as a civilian in the SCP universe.

Perhaps the story could also alternate between perspectives as foundation agents realize there’s a civilian who’s onto them.

I think ultimately the tale would end with the protagonist learning much more than any typical civilian would ever hope to. Like witnessing one or more SCPs firsthand, but getting killed in the process.

Hook/Attention-Grabber: Most tales I’ve read are from the perspective of either Foundation Agents, someone in a GoI, or an SCP. I don’t know of many from the perspective of civilians. I also think the leaks from SCP-2137 are an event ripe for exploration.

And I also try t explore a bit how people who are not exposed to the statue react to it. Sure, the organization tries to contain it, but there might be others who see it as an opportunity.
So beside the basic structure I would present a timeline of the events that led to the capture of the object, and a story in the first person about an attempt to steal it in order to expose a whole SCP facility.
I think presenting it as an addendum works better for one narrative, while presenting it as a story works better for a different narrative.

Hook/Attention-Grabber: Rather than just the danger posed by the anomalous properties themselves I was interested in how the existence of those anomalous properties represent a thought hazard in those who know of them.

Additional Notes: I already wrote it and put it on my sandbox, mostly because I was interested in the idea and wanted to expand it, I would like some feedback and I would like to see if other people would enjoy it a much. It's mostly complete, but there are some things that can change based on feedback.
For instance in my original draft the timeline was more detailed and longer, then I streamlined it to the essentials, but I can expand it again if there's interest in it.

Central Narrative: The SCP Foundation caught wind of the supposed SCP due to a 911 call. As Foundation Agents further investigate the home and family they give contradictory reports. Initial reports show evidence that the home and entities residing in it exhibit anomalous properties. Further reports however state that there is nothing anomalous, and the Agents themselves suddenly become increasingly adamant that everything is perfectly normal and dismiss their own initial evidence which proved otherwise. A field test is done and Agents participating in it conduct separate investigations. All initial investigations during the field test turn up similar evidence of anomalous behavior. Further investigations done by the same agents show no evidence of anomalous behavior, as well as the Agents confidently stating that everything is normal. Foundation researchers hypothesize the home and family may be connected somehow, maybe even being one single entity that tries to keep up its own veil of normality around it for unknown reasons. Initial investigations turn up evidence of an anomaly, but later investigations do not as the SCP "fixes" evidence of its anomalous properties so it doesn't show up again for individual investigators. Individuals investigating are also affected by this "fix." The anomalous effects most likely apply individually. This hypothesis is accepted and the home and family are classified as SCP-XXXX. Anyone investigating or documenting the SCP must work on it only once, and immediately report their findings. All initial evidence has been shown individually and only once to O5-██, O5-██, and the Ethics Committee for confirmation.

Hook/Attention-Grabber: Is this a misunderstanding and the SCP Foundation is investigating a normal family, or is something else going on here?

item.title: Corpse of a Dead God
item.description: This is a redone version of a previous idea thread I had. This is about the mummified corpse of an animalistic humanoid.
item.content:encoded:
Seeking Greenlight: Yes

Page Type: SCP Article

Genre: Horror, History

Page Layout: Containment procedure, description, tests, interview, personal report, final addendum.

Elevator Pitch: SCP-XXXX is a mummified body with a human torso, arms, and head, but it has animalistic legs, a tail, and horns. The mouth and eyelids are closed. It is completely unresponsive to people and could be easily written off as being dead. It has been reported to been speaking Doric Greek, Latin, and a third unknown language. It will never move and is quiet limp, but the body itself will never wither or fall apart, remaining perfectly intact. Flora will emerge in the surrounding area and will continue to grow, and if a dissection is attempted its mouth will snap open and a loud, ear-bleeding scream will emerge from it for a small period of time.

Central Narrative: (From a diary) The body was discovered in a hidden grotto on the island of Paxi in the 1950s. It was bought by the Brazilian ceo of a food processing company, who had a fascination with occult symbols and strange artifacts. The body was accidentally delivered to his hotel room near a deforested site. The next day, the sight was completely regrown. After some more "experiments" he concluded that this body could restore the earth's lost flora and fauna. But instead of using it as a way to fix deforestation, he used it to essentially create infinite resources for his own profit. He saw nothing wrong with this, claiming that if the body didn't want him to prosper, it wouldn't regrow the wild. It came as no surprise by his blue collar workers (who thought he was a witch) when he and the body disappeared, and soon his colleagues and some workers.
The foundation was soon reported and contained the corpse. It unfortunately destroyed its original containment cell and caused the causality of one personal, so it had to be moved to its own site in the end.

Hook/Attention-Grabber: I don't believe there's any SCP quiet like this. It's a mummified corpse that's really a powerful being trapped in pathetically useless body but can still use all of its powers is a literary contradiction but a narratively important one. It explores an interesting side of big business, about how often times they try to mask their destructive actions against nature with claims of the corporation being safe and loving nature and whatnot.

Seeking Greenlights: Yes

Genre (Optional): Horror.

Page Layout (Optional): Standard SCP page layout.

Elevator Pitch: A set of Kodak carousel slide projectors that synchronously display a cognitohazardous set of images.

+ Central Narrative
- hide Central Narrative

Central Narrative: The SCP is a set of four Kodak carousel slide projectors that, despite not sharing any physical linkage, move through their slides in sync with each other. It requires no power and retains its anomalous properties even when disassembled.

The SCP stays inactive for a period of 72 hours, and turns on for 35 minutes, cycling through a set of 450 slides, despite each projector only being capable of holding 140 slides.

The first 15 slides are what are assumed to be testing slides, and display no anomalous effects. The next set of 185 slides appears differently to each observer, and are personalized, latching onto observers' subconscious anxieties and fears. Besides this, this set has the cognitohazardous quality of being impossible to walk away from — once the first slide in the set is seen, the observer cannot look away from it on their own.

If any one of the observers carries with them regret involving a dead loved one, the SCP moves onto the next set of slides. If not, then the slides end early and it goes back into its 72-hour dormant stage, ending the cognitohazardous effect.

Only observers with regret deemed significant enough by the SCP will be held on to by the cognitohazardous effect, still unable to look away. It is assumed that what is projected is a set of instructions detailing the construction of a SCP-XXXX-02, a coffin-like chamber. An observer who finishes watching the slideshow through will become obsessed with constructing this chamber, and will use every tool in their disposal in order to do so. Once they finish construction, they will attempt to obtain any remains of their dead loved ones, and enter the chamber with them. The chamber then attempts to combine the two things that enter, breaking after one use. As the only subjects tested have been D-Classes with minimal construction knowledge, their chambers were constructed shoddily and resulted in poor amalgamations.

To all other observers, the projectors appear to be projecting only white. It is unknown what exactly the schematics are, as the chamber completely deconstructs and the materials requested by the D-Class seem to disappear off of recordings and logs once the chamber expires.

Hook/Attention-Grabber: I always find SCPs involving twists on normal objects interesting, and old-school slide projectors pop up in horror more than you'd think, so it seemed a good fit.

item.title: SCP Idea: Dynaroo
item.description: A strong Kangaroo attacks the Foundation
item.content:encoded:
Seeking Greenlights: No

Page Type: SCP Article

Elevator Pitch: A large, angry, and buff kangaroo with a personal grudge against the SCP Foundation goes from an amusing anomaly to becoming a terrifying threat.

Narrative/Hook +
Narrative/Hook -

Central Narrative: The Foundation receives reports of a very large Kangaroo ambushing D-class transports and holding facilities in Australia. Attempts to capture the Kangaroo fail as it only appears to free D-class and kill Foundation staff before disappearing, and it won’t fall for set-ups or traps. Staff’s first response is amusement at the idea of their "Looney Tunes"-esque rivalry. However, by the end, that’s contrasted by a video-log transcript where staff on a D-class transport bus are terrified at the sight of it on the horizon, coming for them.

After 2 years of failure to contain him, the Kangaroo is suddenly found in the wild and is easily captured. When the head researcher appears on-site to see the contained SCP from an observation booth, the Kangaroo assassinates the doctor with a powerful kick that kills him, the nearby staff, and destroys the containment chamber. He escapes, revealing he let the Foundation capture him in order to kill the researcher in charge of his containment.

They then discover that a D-class that escaped years ago left a record of his time in the Australian outback while on the run. After punching him out of fear, the D-class begins to bond with a rogue male Kangaroo. Over several weeks, the D-class and the Kangaroo become close companions. After a night of realizing his inevitable doom, the D-class told the Kangaroo all the secrets he knew about the Foundation as a small way to rebel against the unbeatable odds. He was eventually found and terminated by Agents who neglected to terminate the lone witness, the Kangaroo.

The Agents involved are discovered to be MIA and the same researcher who approved the termination is revealed to be the same one who became the head researcher that was assassinated. The Foundation theorizes that either the researcher was simply too careless to make the connection, or something/someone else knew and was assisting the Kangaroo in his quest for revenge.

Hook/Attention-Grabber: The absurdity will make you laugh, but by emphasizing the reality of the physical strength in actual kangaroos will this SCP make you terrified. By slowly escalating the serious tone of the article, the reader realizes along with the Foundation how much they underestimated this anomaly.


Additional Notes: There will be no references to the 2003 film “Kangaroo Jack” in the article whatsoever.

Promise.

This SCP aims to somewhat alleviate that. A series of instructions, warnings, one-time-use spells, etc, etc given to the victims of these anomalous incidents (just a portion of them, enough to catch the Foundation's attention) to help them escape the situation unharmed. but the reality is often bleaker than it looks.

+ show block

Central Narrative: We are presented with the SCP, the set of requirements for its manifestation. Then, we look through the list of incidents it took place in (about 8 ~ 15 I haven't found the goldilocks number to form a pattern or a narrative yet, officially in the record, it would be around a few thousand). The pattern we see here would be that this SCP has pretty much about 35% success rate with success being the receiver will have no other connection with the anomaly and survive(of course) the rest would be either dead (anomalously or not), sunk deeper into the abnormal, recruited by different GOIs (including the Foundation). Then we are presented with some transcript of the SCP's instruction and we would see some changes in tones, sadder, more pessimistic, although more professional, a stand out transcript would show why it did what it did.

Hook/Attention-Grabber: The audience would be hooked (hopefully) with the question of "What about the average civilian in the world dwelled within the anomaly?" and the methods that this unknown force behind the SCP utilizes to help the victims and how the Foundation apply them to standard protocols.
